name: stack_tally_arithmetic
provenance: direct response to: 'presumably even with unary chains we could teach it stack based arithmetic?' -- and a genuine self-correction: peano_arithmetic.meta.json's pred1 facts were built using REAL SUBTRACTION (i - 1) to generate decimal labels, which is circular for 'teaching it math from nothing' (it presupposes the very arithmetic being bootstrapped). This version represents each number as a TALLY STRING (a stack of marks: "" for 0, "|" for 1, "||" for 2, ...) built by PURE STRING CONCATENATION ONLY -- zero arithmetic involved anywhere in constructing the facts. 'Predecessor' becomes a purely structural relation: one string is the other with exactly one mark popped off the end.

rules.zero: rule zero("v:").  -- the empty tally string
rules.pred1_chain: rule pred1("v:tally(N)", "v:tally(N-1)") -- e.g. rule pred1("v:|||", "v:||").  each built by appending exactly one "|" to the previous string, never by subtracting numbers
rules.plus:
rule plus(A, "v:", A).
rule plus(A, B, C) :- pred1(B, B2), pred1(C, C2), plus(A, B2, C2).  -- IDENTICAL shape to the decimal-label version, confirming the mechanism doesn't care about the numeral system used

significance: proves the relational-chain mechanism works over a genuinely bootstrapped, structure-only number representation, not just because the decimal-label version happened to encode magnitude in its string content -- the SAME plus/pred1 rule definitions, unmodified, work correctly whether numbers are decimal-string labels or tally-mark stacks, confirming the induction/verification mechanism is about RELATIONAL STRUCTURE, not about which numeral system labels the facts.
